why: The note 'The amendments read as follows:' between rules, with no marker, was credited to the member speaking instead of having no speaker. It keeps the turn, so his speech after the second rule keeps its speaker. The two amendment lines inside the rules keep his speaker only because the turn is kept; that is a known residue, not a ruling that he spoke them.

Section Name:BUDGET
Title:BUDGET, MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS
MPs Speaking:Mr Chai Chong Yii (Minister of State for Communications); Mr Yong Nyuk Lin (Minister for Communications); Mr Ang Nam Piau; Mr Cheong Yuen Chee; Mr Chin Harn Tong; Mr Hwang Soo Jin; Mr Ivan Baptist; Mr J. F. Conceicao; Mr L. P. Rodrigo; Mr N. Govindasamy; Mr Ng Kah Ting; Mr P. Govindaswamy; Mr Phey Yew Kok; Mr Sia Khoon Seong; Mr Sim Boon Woo; Mr Teong Eng Siong; Mr Yeo Toon Chia; Dr Yeoh Ghim Seng (Mr Speaker);


Column: 571

MAIN AND DEVELOPMENT ESTIMATES OF SINGAPORE FOR THE

FINANCIAL YEAR 1ST APRIL, 1975 TO 31ST MARCH, 1976



    Mr Yong Nyuk Lin: Mr Speaker, Sir, perhaps the criticisms or queries raised `by the `Members "for Sembawang and Anson on the Singapore Bus Service are items which can really be fully answered

Column: 581

when we come to amendment (2)* which will be moved by the Member for Boon Teck and amendment (6)+ on the Registry of Vehicles.
The amendments read as follows:

    *(2) That the sum -to be allocated for, Head 0 be reduced by $10 in respect of subhead AAA 1901.

    +(6)That the sum to be allocated for Head 0 be reduced by $10 in respect of subhead FAA 1107.


    But the Member for Sembawang raised two other points which I think I can answer now. He mentioned about the progress of the Mass Transit Study. Here again, it comes under amendment (9)* (* The amendment reads as follows:(9) That the sum to be allocated for Head 0 be reduced by $10 in respect of subhead AAA 8101.) and if he wilt be patient enough to wait, we can give him the answer then. But he did mention about the Road Transport Action Committee's policies which are not well received and inquired whether this came within the White Paper on the Reorganisation of the Motor Transport Service of Singapore. I would like to bring to his notice that this White Paper was a three-year plan for the period 1970-73. So it has nothing to do with the Road Transport Action Committee of five Permanent Secretaries, which was appointed in October 1973 after the recommendations of the White Paper have already been more or less accomplished, nor has it anything to do with the follow-up of the recommendations in the White Paper. These are new policies subsequent to the publication of the White Paper.
